A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NegationCLIP method and NegRefCOCOg benchmark. Their main texts and complete appendices, including figures, tables, and equations, are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original training-data analyses, CelebA classification results, fine-tuning experiments and ablations, and text-to-image generation and segmentation evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds COCO retrieval, CoN-CLIP comparisons, comparative CelebA results, and LMD Negation benchmark outcomes.

M1.justification: The two caption-generation pipelines, frozen vision encoder, text-encoder fine-tuning with InfoNCE, and encoder substitution in diffusion and segmentation models remain unchanged. Sections 3 and 4.1 and Appendix C describe the same proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds general COCO caption-to-image retrieval evaluation; COCO previously served as a training source. Appendix F.2 also adds LMD's generic scene-without-object prompts within the existing object-negation generation domain. Training sources and other task coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 adds CoN-CLIP across three architectures in Table 2, SD-1.4 generation in Table 4, segmentation in Table 5, and CelebA in Appendix E.1. Table 12 additionally compares against SD+LMD. These substantially broaden direct comparisons beyond the retained CLIP and CLIP-bnl baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 substantively revises Neg Score: v1 checks only concept absence, whereas v2 requires both subject presence and concept absence. v2 also introduces COCO recall@5 evaluation and a ten-prompt, object-detector-based LMD evaluation. Existing training splits, hyperparameters, and segmentation thresholds remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The CelebA diagnostic changes from reporting 40 attribute-level accuracies in Table 10 to aggregate comparisons involving NegationCLIP and CoN-CLIP in Appendix E.1, removing the detailed performance breakdown. Pipeline ablations in Tables 3 and 7 and the qualitative failure examples remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random seeds per prompt and averaged scores for the 107-prompt generation evaluation. v2 adds no confidence intervals, significance tests, or revised repeated-run practice; it supplies no separate run-count information for the added LMD evaluation.

E6.justification: Under the revised metric, Table 4 replaces SD-1.4's CLIP/NegationCLIP Neg Scores of 0.310/0.464 with 0.295/0.449, and SDXL's 0.314/0.484 with 0.308/0.421; these are not same-setting performance declines. v2 adds COCO and CoN-CLIP results, CelebA accuracies of 64.0% for NegationCLIP and 60.6% for CoN-CLIP, and LMD results of 20%, 94%, and 100% for SD, SD with NegationCLIP, and SD+LMD. Table 10 removes all 40 attribute accuracies. Previously reported Table 2 entries and ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 5.1 revises the binary definition underlying Neg Score from an indicator of concept absence to an indicator requiring both subject presence and concept absence. The mathematical patch constraints in Appendix D remain unchanged, and no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The introduction newly claims that NegRefCOCOg is the first text-to-image retrieval benchmark for evaluating VLM negation comprehension. v1 presented it as a more diverse benchmark extension. The central claims about negation-aware fine-tuning, retained generality, and downstream applications remain stable.

C2.justification: v2 attributes advantages over CoN-CLIP to generating captions grounded in images rather than retrieving images for generated captions. It adds a qualification about subjective CelebA attributes and explains why object-detector evaluation misses action and attribute negation. Existing discussion of difficult generation prompts is retained in Appendix G.

D1.justification: Appendix E.3 and Table 11 add the subject-presence questions and expected answer pairs for the retained generation prompts. Appendices E.3–E.4 document CoN-CLIP encoder substitutions for SD-1.4 and CLIPSeg. Existing training configurations, hardware information, and access information are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around CoN-CLIP, benchmark shortcuts in CREPE Negate and CC-Neg, and prompt preprocessing in LMD. It adds references to SugarCREPE, CREPE, CoN-CLIP, LMD, and self-correcting LLM-controlled diffusion. Sections 1, 3.3, and 6 and Appendix F now distinguish the work from directly relevant general negation approaches and evaluation alternatives.

P1.justification: The introduction, benchmark motivation, main-results discussion, and related work receive targeted rewrites. v2 adds an expanded T2I discussion as Appendix F and moves the existing qualitative discussion to Appendix G. Most method exposition and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains comparator rows and a COCO column and moves earlier; Tables 4–5 gain rows. Table 10 loses its accuracy column, Table 11 gains subject-question columns, and Table 12 is new. Figures retain their examples with limited sizing and diagram-label adjustments; supplementary headings and float placement also change.

improvement.justification: The subject-presence requirement closes a loophole in v1's generation scoring, while CoN-CLIP comparisons and COCO retrieval strengthen empirical support. These benefits are partly offset by removing CelebA's attribute breakdown and introducing a reporting inconsistency: v2 retains the claim of an SDXL gain above 0.15, although Table 4 gives 0.421 minus 0.308, or 0.113. The net improvement is limited but supported.
